correctness.rationale: Canonical minimal rotation yields exactly the rotation-class input/output universes, deletion shadows invariant under representative rotation. Independently reconstructed all binary necklace universes for n=1..9, including the empty output at n=1. Exact BigInt rational inequalities verified all nine feasible disjoint-shadow code witnesses, each output-shadow dual cover n<=8 matching code size, and at n=9 each of 36 fractional packing capacities plus all 60 fractional covering inequalities at common value 41/4. The provided nine-code has pairwise disjoint shadows; each of 19 specified conflict-graph sets is a genuine clique, and their nonnegative rational cover weights >=1 at every vertex with sum 59/6<10. Thus every integral independent set has <=9 elements, while supplied size-nine code is feasible; this is an exact finite proof with both LP sides, not a floating-point solver output. This separately rederived arithmetic from the fetched certificates.json, not just VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The necklace quotient is a natural unrooted circular synchronization/deletion channel, unlike ordinary linear-word deletion codes. The first explicit strict gap between natural shadow-capacity LP and real code size reveals a structural obstruction the fractional formulation misses; rational primal/dual and conflict-clique witnesses make the precise n=9 threshold reproducible and theoretically useful. An exact finite obstruction qualifies without a conjecture about all n.

final_claim: For binary necklaces under one deletion with both input/output quotiented by rotation, optimal integer and fractional output-shadow packings agree for n=1..8 with capacities (1,2,2,3,3,5,6,8); at n=9 they first differ: A_9=9 and F_9=41/4.
limitations: Only binary strings modulo rotations (not reversal/complement), exactly one deletion, and lengths n<=9.
Correctness and finite checks do not establish external mathematical certification or historical priority. No stronger experimental or formal-verification conclusion is drawn.
